needs: dprod:deadline (relative, per-instance PT30S and one P14D)
profile conflict default (odrl:conflict odrl:prohibit on the DPROD profile)
notes: Extracted unchanged except the five anonymous rules are named rule:risk-*. odrl:conflict is absent as in DPROD, so the profile default (odrl:prohibit) applies. Three structural points. First, the delivery duty recurs every minute with a PT30S deadline, and unlike dprod-customer-api-v2 the anchor default matters in the other direction: activation defaults to effective_at, and every instant is a MINUTELY occurrence, so the first evaluation already owes the instance at effective_at itself (due2-workflows.md §5.3). Second, rule:risk-timeliness carries a constraint on a request-source operand — inside a duty that is a guard read against the request (§5.2), so the conformance obligation is in force only for requests whose timeliness is real-time; DPROD never evaluates it, because conformTo never matches the requested action and step 1 collects no duty (§7.2). Third, there is no prohibition, so a Deny can only come from violations = deny. DPROD's expand is clock-anchored with no DTSTART and performed has no lower bound (§8.2); where scenarios supply activation, dprod_expected assumes the same occurrences and Σ produced from the same evidence (exception 2). Intended §7.4 reading throughout.

scenarios.name: real-time display, first evaluation

expected.why: rule:risk-display is unconstrained and ready: Permit. All three obligations are in force. The delivery duty's anchor defaults to effective_at, and 09:05:00 is itself a MINUTELY occurrence — the rule generates every minute — so exactly one instance is owed, at 09:05, its 30-second window open: outstanding. This is the opposite of dprod-customer-api-v2 scenario 1, where the anchor default was not an occurrence and nothing was owed yet. The timeliness guard holds (real-time), so the conformance obligation is in force, with no witness: outstanding. The notification's P14D runs from activation = effective_at: outstanding.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (no prohibition exists; no duty is collected for a display)

scenarios.name: display of non-real-time data

expected.why: Permit as in scenario 1 — the timeliness constraint sits on the conformance obligation, not on the display permission, so it never gates the read. The guard is false (batch ≠ real-time), so rule:risk-timeliness is not in force and is not reported: the SLA is not owed for non-real-time data. Delivery and notification are in force and outstanding as before.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (the duty is not collected, so its condition is never evaluated; the permission is unconstrained)

scenarios.name: timeliness not stated

expected.why: The permission is unconstrained: Permit, whatever the data's freshness. The timeliness operand is missing, so the conformance obligation's guard is U and it is in force with unknown status — reported, not silently dropped. A U guard on an obligation never touches the verdict under violations = ignore; here there is also no deny configuration at all.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (the duty is not collected, so the missing operand never surfaces — due2 reports the unknown, DPROD never looks)

scenarios.name: two minutes missed under DPROD-faithful deny

expected.why: Anchored at 09:00, the per-minute rule yields 09:00, 09:01, 09:02, 09:03 by effective_at, each with a 30-second deadline. ex:ev-delivery-0900 at 09:00:20 witnesses the first: fulfilled. The 09:01 and 09:02 instances have no witness and their deadlines are past: violated. The 09:03 instance's window is open: outstanding. Under violations = deny, a violated instance of an obligation in force denies the display — the SLA has teeth in due2. The conformance and notification obligations are in force and outstanding as in scenario 1.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (deliver never matches display, so no duty is collected and no violation denies — exception 6)
